patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports feeling weaker over the past few months and notices unintentional weight loss. She denies any recent infections, bleeding, or changes in urination. She mentions a previous blood workup indicating elevated BUN and creatinine levels.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Hypertension treated with medication. Father had kidney stones.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol use. Works as an accountant.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate the patient for the cause of anemia, weight loss, and deteriorating renal function.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Over the past few months I’ve felt progressively weaker and I’ve lost weight without trying. I also had some previous bloodwork that showed elevated BUN and creatinine, and my father had kidney stones. I don’t have any urinary symptoms, fever, or bleeding.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any swelling in my joints. It’s mainly been gradual weakness and unintentional weight loss, and I’m not having fever or bleeding either.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp. It’s mostly been the gradual weakness and unintentional weight loss.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had itching or any persistent urge to scratch anywhere on my body.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble raising your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Raising my arms above my head feels more difficult than before—I can do it, but it’s tiring and doesn’t feel as strong as it used to.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any loss of vision or any vision changes that came on without pain. My main issues have been the gradual weakness, the unintentional weight loss, and feeling more easily fatigued when lifting my arms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever, especially nothing that’s been that high or made me feel dizzy or extremely uncomfortable. It’s been more of a gradual weakness, unintentional weight loss, and getting tired more easily—especially when lifting my arms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately. It’s been more a gradual decline in strength and energy, along with unintentional weight loss.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate, and I haven’t noticed any change in urination. It’s mainly the gradual weakness, unintentional weight loss, and tiring more easily, especially when raising my arms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills. It’s been pretty steadily just the gradual weakness and unintentional weight loss, and I tire more easily, especially when I lift my arms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breasts that feel fixed or don’t move. My concern has mostly been the gradual weakness, unintentional weight loss, and getting tired more easily when I lift my arms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had pain or discomfort on the side of my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips. It’s mainly been the gradual weakness, unintentional weight loss, and getting tired more easily when lifting my arms.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t felt any pain in my calf when I walk—there’s nothing that clearly improves when I stop and rest. My problem is more general: I’ve been getting progressively weaker and I’ve lost weight without trying, and lifting my arms tires me out faster than before.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual, and I haven’t had any changes in how often or how it feels when I urinate.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No—moving my arms up or across my body is difficult mainly because it feels like I don’t have as much strength as before. I can still lift and move my arms, but it tires me out faster and feels weaker over time.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your joints feel sore or stiff after doing the same activity repeatedly, like after a long day of typing, lifting, or other repetitive motions?
turns.patient_answer: “No, my joints themselves don’t feel sore or stiff after repetitive activity like typing or lifting. It’s more a generalized weakness and fatigue that comes on gradually, especially when I try to raise my arms.”
